# Story 2fa.1: Enrol an authenticator app
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder, I want to enrol an authenticator app by scanning a QR code and confirming one generated code, so that 2FA only turns on once I have proven my device generates valid codes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a signed-in user with 2FA not enabled, when they start enrolment, then a QR code encoding a new TOTP secret is shown.
- AC-2: Given a user who has started enrolment, when they submit the code currently shown by their authenticator app, then enrolment completes and 2FA is enabled on their account.
- AC-3: Given a user who has started enrolment, when they submit an incorrect code, then enrolment does not complete and 2FA stays disabled.
- AC-4: Given a user who has scanned the QR code but not yet confirmed a code, when they next sign in with their password, then they are not asked for a TOTP code.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Add the `totp_secret` column to the users table (AC: 2, 4)
- [ ] Generate a pending TOTP secret and render it as a QR code on the enrolment page (AC: 1)
- [ ] Verify the submitted code against the pending secret with pyotp; on success, persist `totp_secret` and enable 2FA (AC: 2)
- [ ] On an incorrect code, show an error and leave 2FA disabled (AC: 3)
- [ ] Hold the pending secret in the session until confirmation so an unconfirmed enrolment writes nothing to the users table (AC: 4)

## Dev Notes
- FR-1 is the requirement behind this story.
- Constraint: the existing Flask session-cookie login is the only auth path, and TOTP checks use pyotp with no new service (architecture: verification).
- Constraint: the architecture adds only `totp_secret` to the users table, so "enrolment is complete only on confirmation" is met by keeping the pending secret in the session and writing `totp_secret` on confirmation, not by adding a status column.

### References
- [Source: docs/prd.md#FR-1]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#data-model]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#verification]

# Story 2fa.2: Require a TOTP code at sign-in
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder with 2FA enabled, I want sign-in to require a valid TOTP code after my password, so that a stolen password alone is not enough to access my account.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a user with 2FA enabled, when they submit the correct password, then they are asked for a TOTP code and are not yet signed in.
- AC-2: Given the TOTP code prompt, when they submit the code currently shown by their authenticator app, then they are signed in.
- AC-3: Given the TOTP code prompt, when they submit an invalid code, then they are not signed in and see an error.
- AC-4: Given a user without 2FA enabled, when they submit the correct password, then they are signed in without a TOTP prompt.
- AC-5: Given a user with 2FA enabled, when they submit an incorrect password, then they are not asked for a TOTP code.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Split the login flow so the session is marked authenticated only after the second step succeeds (AC: 1, 2)
- [ ] Add the TOTP code prompt and verify the submitted code with pyotp (AC: 2, 3)
- [ ] Show the TOTP prompt only after the password matches an account with an enabled `totp_secret` (AC: 1, 4)
- [ ] Keep the password-failure path unchanged so no TOTP prompt appears for a wrong password (AC: 5)

## Dev Notes
- FR-2 is the requirement behind this story.
- Constraint: the second step is added to the existing Flask session-cookie login, with pyotp for verification and no new service (architecture: verification). It depends on `totp_secret` from story 2fa.1.

### References
- [Source: docs/prd.md#FR-2]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#verification]

# Story 2fa.3: Recover sign-in with recovery codes
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an account holder, I want ten single-use recovery codes issued when I enrol, so that I can still sign in if I lose my authenticator device.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a user who has just completed enrolment, when enrolment completes, then they are shown exactly ten recovery codes.
- AC-2: Given the TOTP prompt at sign-in, when they submit any one of their ten recovery codes, then they are signed in.
- AC-3: Given the TOTP prompt at sign-in, when they submit a recovery code that has already been used, then they are not signed in and see an error.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Generate ten recovery codes at enrolment and store them in the `recovery_codes` column (AC: 1)
- [ ] Show the ten codes to the user when enrolment completes (AC: 1)
- [ ] Accept any unused recovery code in place of a TOTP code and mark that code as used (AC: 2)
- [ ] Reject a recovery code that has already been used (AC: 3)

## Dev Notes
- FR-3 is the requirement behind this story.
- Constraint: the architecture adds `recovery_codes` to the users table (architecture: data-model), so each code's used state must persist there to survive restarts and session changes.
- Constraint: codes are consumed at the same TOTP prompt added in story 2fa.2, and issued at the enrolment confirmation point from story 2fa.1.

### References
- [Source: docs/prd.md#FR-3]
- [Source: docs/architecture.md#data-model]

- [ ] Accept an unused recovery code at the TOTP prompt in place of a TOTP code and mark it used (AC: 2, 4)

# Story 1.3: Rate-limit counters survive an application restart
Status: ready-for-dev

## Story
As an API operator, I want rate-limit counters to survive an application restart, so that restarting the service does not give every client a fresh budget.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AC-1: Given a client has used part of its budget in the current window, when the application restarts, then the client's next request counts against the budget it already used, not a fresh one.
- AC-2: Given a client has exhausted its limit in the current window, when the application restarts, then its next request is still rejected with 429 and a Retry-After header.
- AC-3: Given a client's window has fully elapsed, when it sends a request, then its budget resets as normal.

## Tasks / Subtasks
- [ ] Hold per-key counters in Redis instead of process memory so they are not lost on restart (AC: 1, 2)
- [ ] Give each counter a TTL equal to its window so counters reset on schedule (AC: 3)
- [ ] Verify by restarting the application mid-window and checking that the count carries over (AC: 1, 2)

## Dev Notes
- CAP-1 is the requirement behind this story. Redis is the intended counter store, so the counters are kept there; process memory would reset on every restart.
- Architecture constraint: Redis is already in the stack and is the intended counter store (`counter-store`).
